title: Balance patch proposals for your review
summary: Review these proposals together: reducing early mastery acceleration, recurring free acquisitions and Tetra's damage may change how much help Volos and the weaker destinies need. The four recommended candidates form the proposed core patch. The Giga price change is an alternative to its mastery reduction, never an additional nerf in this version. Experimental entries and decisions to retain current rules are separately reviewable. No rules have been changed. The evidence comes from one AI policy, so card strength and the AI's choices cannot be fully separated; the proposed numbers are hypotheses, not measured post-patch results.

cohort.format: Duel, Nyou Haïai with search on both sides
cohort.matchups: 189 games in each of the 20 ordered matchups of different heroes; no mirrors
cohort.validation_plan: After the review, define the intended package and its acceptable balance range. Compare baseline, individual changes and their combination on paired seeds with both starting seats. Track hero matchups, relic choices and rewards, opening-card availability, victory routes and game-length tails. Give the policy an opportunity to adapt before treating the result as final balance; self-play's aggregate win rate is always 50% and is not a patch success metric.

groups.title: Recommended core patch
groups.description: The four clearest tuning candidates. They are linked: the Brain change reduces damage pressure, the Giga change slows one mastery engine, Deadly Recruits loses free tempo, and Crown improves Volos's cycling. Their combined effect still needs validation.

groups.title: Alternative to a core change
groups.description: An either-or choice for Giga. Choose the mastery reduction or the price increase; stacking both would make it harder to tell whether the card was overcorrected.

groups.title: Optional changes with weaker evidence
groups.description: Concrete designs to review alongside the core package. These are not included in the recommended core by default. The weak-card observations may partly reflect AI selection or timing mistakes.

groups.title: Keep current rules and monitor
groups.description: Explicit decisions you can also challenge. Strong-looking opening cards, rare relics and global rules should be reassessed after the chosen package rather than receiving automatic additional nerfs or buffs.

proposals.title: Giga: Dominion mastery 3 → 2
proposals.confidence: Strong imbalance signal; moderate confidence in this tuning
proposals.current: Cost 2, defense 4. When played, draw 1 card. Exhaust — Dominion: gain 3 mastery.
proposals.proposed: In Duel only, change the Dominion exhaust to gain 2 mastery. Keep cost 2, defense 4 and the draw on play. Add a Duel replacement so the original card remains unchanged in other formats.
proposals.reason: Reduce a cheap champion's repeated mastery acceleration while preserving its identity and accessibility. This is the strongest opening outlier supported by both acquisition and initial-market evidence. A normal purchase puts Giga into discard; the draw is on playing it, not on buying it.
evidence: Giga was in the initial market in 117 games. The first player acquired it in all 117 and won 82, or 70.1%; first-player wins were 51.1% when Giga was absent.
The initial-offer association remains about +18.1 percentage points after controlling hero matchup and both opening hands' buying power; the 95% interval is +9.4 to +26.8 points.
Players acquiring Giga by round 2 won 145/206 games, or 70.4%. Successful Dominion triggers were not logged, so the exact contribution of each activation remains unknown.

interactions.text: Mutually exclusive alternative: do not also raise Giga's price in this proposed version.

Giga slows mastery acceleration while Brain reduces damage before mastery 20. These changes pull victory routes in opposite directions; judge their combined effect rather than assuming both simply slow every game.
Crown's improved cycling may help Volos recover mastery tempo lost through Giga. Check that the package does not merely transfer the strongest mastery route to one hero.
Keep the other early Order engines intact initially; stacking broad mastery nerfs risks suppressing the entire strategy.

watch: Initial-market Giga advantage and early purchase rate
Successful Dominion triggers and mastery 10/20/30 timing
Rez's matchups and the overall share of mastery victories
Round distribution, including unusually early finishes

proposals.title: Deadly Recruits: activation costs 1 gem
proposals.confidence: Strong selection signal; moderate confidence in the amount
proposals.current: Exhaust for no gem cost: choose an ally in the market costing 2 or less, then fast-play it OR recruit it for free. At mastery 20, the limit becomes 4.
proposals.proposed: Pay 1 gem and exhaust to use the same fast-play-or-recruit choice. Retain the cost-2 limit below mastery 20 and cost-4 limit from mastery 20 onward. The payment is an activation cost, not an additional price charged for the selected card.
proposals.reason: Charge for repeatable access to immediate effects or permanent cards. Reducing only recruitment would miss the principal observed use, which is fast-play. One gem could be too severe for an already conditional market-dependent action, so its choice and usage rates matter.
evidence: Normal selectors won 64.5% of 752 games. The association remains about +11.0 percentage points after matchup, seat and selection-timing adjustment.
Of 3,043 recorded mode choices, 2,554 were fast-play and 489 recruit: approximately 84% fast-play.
The favorable raw result appears across all five heroes, although choosing the destiny remains a strategic, nonrandom event.

interactions.text: Fewer free plays may already reduce Brain's faction access and cycling. Applying both can reduce Tetra's output more than either change alone.
Conscription rewards cheap allies and can benefit from Deadly Recruits when extra destinies are obtained. Making its condition easier should not recreate an excessive free-action package.
J-Chord still offers repeatable free fast-plays. Track whether it becomes the dominant substitute before nerfing both engines.
The new gem cost competes with Focus and ordinary purchases, potentially slowing mastery even though this change does not directly change mastery output.

watch: Choice rate when this destiny is available
Paid activations, eligible targets and successful fast-play/recruit resolutions
Pre-mastery-20 usefulness versus other destinies
Power, mastery and permanent-card value gained per activation

proposals.title: Multitask Brain: pre-mastery-20 power per faction 2 → 1
proposals.confidence: Strong Tetra signal; moderate confidence in the relic attribution
proposals.current: For each distinct faction played this turn, gain 2 power and draw 1 card. At mastery 20, gain 4 power per faction instead. The faction count is evaluated before these draws.
proposals.proposed: Below mastery 20, gain 1 power and draw 1 card per distinct faction played. At mastery 20, retain 4 power and 1 draw per faction. Keep Tetra's hero power unchanged.
proposals.reason: Reduce the damage attached to Tetra's exceptionally strong draw engine without removing her cycling identity. This halves the relic's early power, a substantial change; retaining the mastery-20 reward gives the build a later payoff.
evidence: Tetra wins 876/1,512 games, or 57.9%, and leads against every opposing hero. Ordinary damage accounts for 77.7% of her wins.

Brain is 90.1% of Tetra's normal relic choices; those games win 734/1,190, or 61.7%. The timing-adjusted association is similar, but hero power, relic choice and deck quality are not causally separated.

A normal Brain play supplies its own Order faction. Prism can supply all five factions, giving the current card a maximum of 10 power plus 5 draws below mastery 20. The proposal lowers that maximum to 5 power plus 5 draws; mastery-20 output stays 20 power plus 5 draws.

interactions.text: Reaching Brain's unchanged high tier could become slower after Giga's nerf. Conversely, lower early damage gives both sides more time to pursue mastery.
Charging for free fast-plays can reduce faction coverage and draw chains before Brain resolves, compounding its direct power reduction.
Less Tetra damage may already improve Volos's Crown route. A Crown buff on top could be larger than its isolated result suggests.
Watch whether Tetra moves to Terminal Crescents; its high raw win rate is dominated by multiple-relic games and is not a sound reason to nerf it simultaneously.

watch: Every Tetra matchup and both starting seats
Brain output per faction, tier and play
Switching to other relics
Late mastery wins, long games and the size of the mastery-20 power jump

proposals.title: Panconscious Crown: add Draw 1
proposals.confidence: Strong route weakness; uncertain rules-versus-policy cause
proposals.current: Gain 2 mastery and 5 health. Then, at mastery 20, Unify grants another 50 health. Crown's own mastery gain can reach the threshold before the check.
proposals.proposed: Retain the existing mastery and healing effects, then draw 1 card after those effects resolve. Placing the draw last preserves the present Unify check. Do not increase First Aid or Entropic Talons at the same time.
proposals.reason: Help a weak relic route cycle into its payoff instead of adding more healing to games it already prolongs. This is the core proposal with the largest interaction concern: improving consistency can strengthen an already explosive Crown-plus-Talons deck.
evidence: Crown selectors win 95/299 games, or 31.8%, versus 485/998, or 48.6%, for Talons. The large gap persists after measured selection and mastery timing adjustment.
Crown players reach mastery 20 in 59.5% of games, yet average 10.96 rounds and frequently fail to finish. Volos already reaches mastery 10 most often, so earlier access is not the obvious bottleneck.

Volos acquired both Crown and Talons in 75 games and won 60, or 80.0%. These selected reward-enriched decks do not establish a causal combo win rate. Mechanically, Talons before Crown can convert Crown's 5 + 50 healing into 55 power, even at full health.

interactions.text: Reducing Tetra's early damage could already give Crown enough time to win. Review the combined benefit before assuming the full draw buff remains necessary.
The draw helps Crown cycle toward mastery 30 while the Giga change slows a shared mastery source; compare these effects by hero.
More reliable healing also becomes more reliable Talons power. Test these healing changes with every relic source, including additional relic rewards.
Keep the 55-power interaction visible as a separate design decision. This proposal leaves that rule intact; it is not evidence that the combo needs a further buff.

watch: Crown selected alone versus acquired alongside Talons
Same-turn relic order and healing converted to power, including at full health
Mastery-30 conversion, long-game tail and Volos matchups
Whether better relic selection alone removes the apparent weakness

proposals.title: Alternative Giga tuning: cost 2 → 3
proposals.confidence: Strong card signal; less direct mechanism target
proposals.current: Giga costs 2, has defense 4, draws 1 on play and exhausts for Dominion: gain 3 mastery.
proposals.proposed: Instead of reducing mastery, make Duel Giga cost 3. Retain defense 4, Draw 1 on play and Dominion mastery 3. Do not combine this with the core Giga mastery reduction in this version.
proposals.reason: This preserves the later engine and charges more opening tempo. It is an alternative if the intended identity is a powerful mastery champion purchased at a more meaningful opportunity cost.
evidence: The same initial-market and early-acquisition evidence underlying the core Giga proposal applies.
Every first-seat opening hand in this cohort can generate at least 3 gems. A price increase to 3 would therefore not prevent an opening purchase; it would compete with Focus and other purchases.
The effect of a price change was not simulated and cannot be inferred as a precise win-rate reduction from the existing games.

interactions.text: Choose one Giga proposal. This is a replacement, not an additional nerf.
Both price changes put pressure on gem budgets. They can reduce Focus use indirectly even while printed mastery effects are unchanged.
Decima's discount and each hero's spending priorities can make the higher price affect heroes differently.

watch: First-turn Giga purchases and the second purchase/Focus given up
Per-hero effective purchase prices
Mastery acceleration after Giga enters play
Whether initial-offer advantage remains excessive despite the extra gem

proposals.title: Unconditional Conscription: one cheap ally for 2 power
proposals.confidence: Moderate weakness signal; low confidence in this redesign
proposals.current: Exhaust: if you played at least 2 non-starter allies costing 2 or less this turn, gain 4 power. The current engine checks played non-starter, non-champion cards at printed cost 2 or less; qualifying non-champion relics also count.
proposals.proposed: In Duel, require at least 1 qualifying card instead of 2 and grant 2 power instead of 4. Retain the existing eligibility test, including its treatment of relics. This is a reliability redesign with a lower ceiling, not an unconditional power buff.
proposals.reason: Make a small aggressive reward usable on ordinary turns rather than requiring two cheap cards together. Measure successful triggers first: the existing low win rate may partly reflect the AI taking a poor leftover destiny or choosing it too late.
evidence: Normal selectors won 178/424 games, or 42.0%; the adjusted association is about -7.9 percentage points.
First-seat selectors won 72/210, or 34.3%, while second-seat selectors won 106/214, or 49.5%. Their average selection rounds differ, reinforcing the timing and choice concern.
Activation counters do not reveal how often the current condition successfully paid out.

interactions.text: A cheaper condition may partly offset fewer free cheap-card plays, including decks that obtain both destinies.
More reliable small damage could compensate for reduced Brain damage without restoring its large draw-plus-power burst.
Cheap Order allies can already support this condition. Do not interpret stronger Conscription results as independent proof those cards need another nerf.

watch: Eligible turns, successful triggers and total power per game
Effect of non-champion relics satisfying the condition
Destiny options still available at selection
Choice and performance by seat and selection round

proposals.title: Soul Syphon: two factions for 5 health
proposals.confidence: Moderate weakness signal; low confidence in this redesign
proposals.current: Exhaust: if you played at least 3 faction-bearing cards spanning at least 3 different factions this turn, gain 7 health. The separate card-count gate prevents a lone Prism from meeting the condition.
proposals.proposed: Require at least 2 faction-bearing cards spanning at least 2 factions, and heal 5 instead of 7. Keep the minimum-card gate aligned with the faction requirement, so a lone Prism still does not qualify.
proposals.reason: Trade a larger conditional heal for more frequent modest healing. This may improve ordinary damage matchups but cannot answer an Infinity finish; if mastery defeats explain most losses, easier healing may fail to solve the actual problem.
evidence: Normal selectors win 44.5% of 539 games; the adjusted association is about -7.1 percentage points.
The existing logs do not identify successful Soul Syphon triggers or healing converted to power by source.
No tested hero-by-initial-destiny-offer interaction survives multiple-testing correction, so this is not established as a problem confined to one hero.

interactions.text: Talons can convert this healing into power even at full health. Combining greater healing reliability with better Crown cycling may create a stronger Volos damage route.
Lower early damage makes healing relatively less urgent and can shift games toward mastery, which bypasses its main defensive benefit.
Monitor game-length tails and damage-versus-mastery victories before adding several defensive changes together.

watch: Condition success rate and healing actually restored
Healing converted to power, especially through Talons
Damage defeats versus mastery defeats
Destiny choice rate and longer-game frequency

proposals.title: Furrowing Elemental: cost 5 → 4
proposals.confidence: Low; small early sample and purchase-timing bias
proposals.current: Cost 5, Undergrowth ally. Gain 4 health and draw 1 card; then, if at 50 health, gain 4 power. There are 2 copies.
proposals.proposed: Reduce the Duel card's cost to 4. Retain both copies and all effects, including checking full health after its healing and draw resolve.
proposals.reason: Test whether the card asks too much economy for a conditional damage payoff. The alternative explanation is simply that this AI buys a defensive midgame card too early, so this is optional rather than part of the recommended core.
evidence: Players acquiring it by round 2 won 19/61 games, or 31.1%. This is a small and strategically selected sample.
A weak early-purchase result does not establish that the card is weak later or when offered in suitable decks.

interactions.text: Cost 4 makes Furrowing newly eligible for Deadly Recruits at mastery 20 and for other cost-4 acquisition effects. The price change therefore affects more than normal gem purchases.
Cheaper Undergrowth healing and draw can support both Crown's Unify and Talons' power conversion.
Reduced incoming damage may make Furrowing's full-health power trigger easier to maintain, further increasing its value.

watch: Normal purchases versus free acquisitions at cost thresholds
Performance when first acquired in early, middle and late rounds
Full-health trigger success
Talons combinations and defensive game length

proposals.title: Optional new card: Aegis Surveyor
proposals.confidence: Design hypothesis only; no games or balance evidence
proposals.current: No such card exists. Current evidence does not require adding a new card to fix the clearest outliers.
proposals.proposed: Optional Duel card concept: Aegis Surveyor, Homodeus ally, cost 3, quantity 2, hand shield 2. Play: gain 2 power; if your mastery is lower than the opponent's when this effect resolves, gain 1 mastery. It has no draw, no mercenary fast-play mode and no champion defense. The ordinary hand-shield rule applies; playing it does not grant a persistent shield.
proposals.reason: Offer a modest defensive purchase that can narrow a mastery deficit without taking mastery away from the leader or changing global thresholds. Keep this outside the core patch: a new card changes market composition and adds a design objective beyond correcting measured outliers.
evidence: When both players reached mastery 10 in different rounds, the earlier player won 68.9%. This motivates exploring catch-up tools but does not prove the threshold itself is unfair.
There is no measured result for this proposed card. Cost, shield, quantity and output are explicit starting design values, not validated balance numbers.

interactions.text: Reducing Giga may already remove enough early mastery disparity. Avoid adding catch-up merely to counter an outlier that the core patch fixes.
Another faction-bearing card can feed Brain and Dominion. Homodeus identity avoids adding another Order card but does not remove multi-faction synergy.
Cost 3 makes it eligible for J-Chord's early Warp even though it is not a paid mercenary fast-play card.
Its defensive value and behind-only mastery should be assessed together for pacing. A card need not make games faster to improve balance.

watch: Purchase frequency while ahead versus behind in mastery
Successful catch-up triggers and shield use
Ability to reverse a lead without creating an incentive to remain behind
Market dilution and effects on faction engines

proposals.title: J-Chord: retain current rules, prioritize a second check
proposals.confidence: Meaningful opening signal; additional nerf not yet justified
proposals.current: Cost 3, defense 3. Exhaust — Warp 3. At mastery 15, Warp 6 instead.
proposals.proposed: Keep these values in the proposed core patch. Recheck its initial-market advantage and successful free-play output after the chosen changes.
proposals.reason: Its opening signal warrants attention, but the package already reduces another recurring free-action engine. Establish whether J-Chord remains excessive or simply becomes a healthy alternative.
evidence: When initially offered in 124 games, first-player wins were 65.3%, versus 51.3% when absent. The adjusted association is about +14.0 percentage points, with a wider interval than Giga's.
The first player acquired it in round 1 in 120 of those 124 games. Early acquisition is also positively associated with winning.

interactions.text: A gem charge on Deadly Recruits increases the relative attractiveness of J-Chord's free activation.
Slower mastery can delay J-Chord's mastery-15 Warp upgrade without changing the card itself.
Any added cost-3 ally changes J-Chord's early target pool.

watch: Initial-offer advantage after the package
Targets available versus successful Warps
Mastery-15 timing
Whether champion removal adequately limits repeated output

proposals.title: Shard Abstractor: retain cost 3 and mastery 2
proposals.confidence: Meaningful opening signal; broad mastery nerf would be premature
proposals.current: Order mercenary, cost 3, quantity 3. Play: gain 2 mastery.
proposals.proposed: Keep its price, quantity and mastery output. Review it again after resolving Giga and the free-acquisition changes, using exact acquisition-mode timestamps.
proposals.reason: Preserve a straightforward paid mastery option while addressing the stronger recurring engine. Its opening association does not establish that first-turn fast-playing it is overpowered.
evidence: With Abstractor in the initial market, first-player wins were 60.2% of 387 games versus 50.8% when absent; the adjusted association is about +10.0 percentage points.
Early acquirers win 57.1% of 613 games. The guaranteed opening-fast-play subset is only 32 player records and wins 53.1%, insufficient to establish a strong positive effect.

interactions.text: Nerfing both sources together could overly penalize mastery-based strategies, especially Rez's observed route.
Abstractor is an eligible cost-3 target for the upgraded destiny at mastery 20; a gem charge already changes that free-value route.
Check each hero, particularly Rez, rather than judging the pooled acquisition rate alone.

watch: Paid recruit, paid fast-play and effect fast-play separately
First-turn opportunity and usage
Mastery wins by hero
Whether its opening advantage persists after Giga's change

proposals.title: Other early engines: no blanket faction or fast-play nerf
proposals.confidence: Positive card signals, insufficient evidence for a combined nerf
proposals.current: Order Initiate, Shard Seer and Duplication Fabricator are associated with good early results. Existing logs mix acquisition modes in first-acquisition timing.
proposals.proposed: Retain their current effects and prices. Keep first-turn fast-play rules unchanged. Improve per-action acquisition-mode and successful-effect logging before making a broader package nerf.
proposals.reason: Do not turn several correlated signs of a strong opening into simultaneous cuts to an entire engine. Brain, Giga and Deadly Recruits already touch faction coverage, mastery, draw and free plays.
evidence: By-round-2 acquisition win rates are 57.1% for Order Initiate, 57.4% for Shard Seer and 57.3% for Duel Fabricator. Their adjusted associations remain positive.
None of 221 tested early card-by-hero interactions or 119 supported early card-pair interactions survives multiple-testing correction.
Lifetime fast-play counts cannot establish the exact mode of the first-round acquisition. The identifiable opening-fast-play subsets provide no convincing positive outlier.

interactions.text: Reducing Giga changes the payoff from Dominion-friendly decks without altering all their components.
The Brain change reduces a major reward for multi-faction draw chains.
A cost on recurring free plays can reduce the same early-engine value indirectly.

watch: Availability-adjusted purchase and fast-play value
Copied effects and successful Dominion triggers
Performance across heroes
Whether several individually reasonable changes combine into an excessive engine nerf

proposals.title: Hero powers: keep all five unchanged initially
proposals.confidence: Good evidence against an emergency Rez or global hero adjustment
proposals.current: At mastery 5: Decima's first-buy discount is 2; Tetra pays 3 gems to draw 2; Volos chooses free heal 3, pay 1 gem for 2 power, pay 2 gems to draw 1, or pay 3 gems for 1 mastery; Ko Syn Wu pays 1 health to banish from hand/discard; Rez can Scry 3 and has a separate passive reducing each reroll's price by 1.
proposals.proposed: Retain every hero power. Address Tetra and Volos through the reviewed relic changes first. In particular, do not add an emergency Rez buff or further increase Doom Gate's monster supply on the basis of older training results.
proposals.reason: The current cohort does not reproduce the old Rez collapse. Simultaneously changing hero powers and their relics would make both interpretation and overshoot harder to manage.
evidence: Hero wins: Tetra 57.9%, Decima 50.1%, Rez 49.3%, Ko Syn Wu 47.6%, Volos 45.0%, each over 1,512 balanced player-games.
Rez uses his ability 6.39 times and rerolls 5.21 times per game. Mastery accounts for 428 of his 745 wins.

Ko's thinning is active, averaging 6.08 starter banishes per game. Decima's zero activation counter is expected for a passive ability. Volos reaches mastery 10 most often, so a starting-mastery buff targets no demonstrated access problem.

interactions.text: The relic nerf may be enough to bring Tetra closer to the field while preserving her hero's draw identity.
Judge Volos's relic adjustment before increasing First Aid or Talons as well.
Rez currently wins mainly through mastery, so reducing early mastery engines can affect him more than his near-even baseline suggests.
If the price alternative is chosen, Decima's discount can change its effective impact.

watch: Full hero matchup matrix rather than only pooled win rates
Successful ability outcomes and opportunities
Relic choice adaptation
Rez's mastery route under the selected package

proposals.title: Rare relics, Doom Gate and finishers: retain current rules
proposals.confidence: Strong evidence of selection bias; weak evidence for more tuning
proposals.current: Rare relic selections and late finishers can show very high raw win rates. Corruption rewards can grant additional relics outside the normal mastery-10 choice.
proposals.proposed: Make no additional changes to these cards in the proposed core patch. Retain Doom Gate's current defense 7 and one-time flood of 35 monsters. Separate single-relic routes, reward relics and same-turn combinations in the next analysis.
proposals.reason: Many apparent winners are already advantaged decks obtaining additional relics, or players acquiring a finisher on their winning turn. Raw ownership win rates are unsuitable nerf targets. The Crown-plus-Talons interaction still deserves explicit review and measurement.
evidence: There are 859 player records with multiple distinct relics. Another relic was acquired in 67/72 Terminal Crescents selections, 22/28 World Piercer selections and 56/85 Unknown God selections.
Praetorian-03's raw advantage over Praetorian-01 disappears after measured selection and mastery timing adjustment.
In 272 Ko games where Doom Gate was played, Ko averaged 2.36 monsters defeated versus 1.11 for the opponent. The evidence does not show that the flood systematically favors his opponent.
High lifetime ownership scores for Comet, Scion and Shadebound include cards acquired immediately before winning.

interactions.text: The potential 55-power Crown/Talons burst means a cycling buff must be evaluated in multiple-relic decks, not only normal Crown selections.
Tetra may switch to Crescents after Brain changes; that supplies more informative normal-choice data than the current tiny standalone sample.
Changing acquisition economy can change both finisher access and the ability to defeat monsters for rewards.

watch: Every relic's acquisition source and chronological use
Normal choices versus reward-enriched decks
Doom Gate rewards for both players
Finisher availability before purchase, not just ownership at victory

proposals.title: Global pacing: retain mastery thresholds and starting compensation
proposals.confidence: Current pacing supports targeted changes first
proposals.current: Normal relic access unlocks at mastery 10 and recruits into discard. Mastery 30 enables Infinity's finishing effect. In a duel both seats start with 5 cards; the second seat also receives 1 mastery and 1 gem for its first turn.
proposals.proposed: Keep mastery 10 and 30, ordinary relic routing, starting hands and second-seat compensation unchanged. Do not add automatic relic-to-hand catch-up, a blanket first-turn fast-play restriction or a global healing nerf in this package.
proposals.reason: The present games already center on ten rounds. First-player advantage is modest overall, while specific opening cards have much larger signals. Fix those candidates before redesigning the game's global race.
evidence: Mean length is 9.98 rounds and median 10; the middle 80% is 8–12 rounds.
First-player wins are 1,955/3,780, or 51.72%, with a 95% interval of 50.13–53.31%.

When both players reach mastery 10 in different rounds, the earlier player wins 68.9%. A one-round lead wins 62.2%, a two-round lead 71.7%, and a lead of at least three rounds 78.9%. These are lead indicators, not isolated causal effects of the threshold.
Current victory routes are 62.4% ordinary damage, 32.3% mastery, 3.7% Comet and 1.6% other health loss.

interactions.text: A targeted mastery-engine reduction can reduce early snowball without delaying every player's relic.
Lower damage may lengthen games or raise the mastery-win share; average length alone cannot decide whether that is healthy.
Crown consistency and defensive optional changes can alter both finishing speed and the long-game tail.
If a behind-mastery mechanic is desired, review it as an explicit design addition rather than an automatic consequence of the 68.9% statistic.

watch: Starting-seat results within each hero matchup
Round distribution and extremely short or long games
Mastery threshold timing with exact action order
Damage, mastery and alternative victory shares
